Local Design Lab · final pass · Health & Billing only

The two that were still wrong

Journey, Attendance, Staff and Care Team are byte-identical to the last pass — verified against the diff, not by inspection. Health & Safety got a real hierarchy; Billing got a real composition. Both got shorter while carrying more.

Health 436 → 379Billing 388 → 294 Panel 2278 → 2126typecheck rc=0

Health & Safety hierarchy 507 × 379 · was 436

Read order is the operator's, not the data model's: critical → care → medication → required documentation → emergency → detail.

Critical is a contained region — the Children --focused treatment in the risk tone, a tint and a rail, not a banner. Multiple critical facts stack inside the one region, so two facts never become two alerts. With none, the region does not render, and nothing says “No alerts”.

Medication nests under the need it supports. An operator understands “asthma, and here is the inhaler for it” — not two lists to cross-reference. Canonical ownership stays separate underneath; this is presentation. A medication with no associated need reads as its own care item.

The header states no summary, because it repeated either the critical region or the HEALTH section below it — the same duplication removed from Billing this pass. Emergency contacts moved to the footer as relationship context. Enrollment health sits in two compact columns and dropped “Received” from its values: inside a section called Enrollment health a date already means received, and the longer string truncated at 190px.

Health specimens A / B / C 253 · 379 · 508

C is the load-bearing specimen: two critical facts, three ongoing needs, four medications, four requirements — and the hierarchy holds. The two critical facts share one region rather than producing two alerts. A, with nothing critical, simply has no region.

Billing recomposed 1023 × 294 · was 388

The header states no money. A summary there duplicated every number in the zones below it and made the card read as malformed. If an amount is past due, the Past Due zone is already the loudest thing on the card.

Payers moved out of the arithmetic into a full-width strip below the zones. As three stacked rows under Current Billing they had made zone one three times the height of the other two; at 1023px, three payers fit on one line.

Recent Ledger is a ledger. Fixed 52 / 1fr / 82 column grid with a quiet Date / Description / Amount heading, uniform 20px rows, tabular figures, right-aligned amounts, no pills. Direction is account balance — a charge or fee increases what is owed (+), a payment, credit, discount or subsidy reduces it (−). The sign carries the meaning; colour only reinforces it.

One correction of substance: the Payment failed  $0 row is gone. A failed payment posts nothing, so it is not a ledger entry — the decline already appears in Past Due, where it is actionable.

Billing specimens A / B / C 282 · 294 · 322

Mixed funding pushes the arithmetic to five lines and the payer strip to three payers — including the funding source, which is a payer like any other. The strip absorbs it because it runs full width. With nothing overdue, Past Due states so calmly rather than disappearing, so the three zones keep their shape.

Three wide cards, one system

Journey 119, Attendance 331, Billing 294 — same header grammar, same in-body section-head grammar, same action treatment, same colour language. Journey and Attendance share the progression band; Billing does not, because its content is arithmetic rather than a sequence. If a fourth wide card ever wants zones, that structure should be promoted to a shared primitive rather than copied.

Locked cards — proof, not assurance

git diff a4cfcc059 over JourneyCard, AttendanceCard, StaffCard, CareTeamCard, ProgressionBand, attendanceDayProjection and CardLabKit returns empty. Health and Billing were built with additive components so no shared primitive changed.
